title: Classical and Folk Dances

cards.h: Dance is a favourite Prelims topic
cards.b: Questions ask which dance belongs to which state, who the exponents are, and what is classical. The Natya Shastra and the Sangeet Natak Akademi are the key reference points.

The Natya Shastra of Bharata (c. 2nd century BCE to 2nd century CE) gives the base: nritta (pure dance), nritya (expressive dance), natya (drama); abhinaya (expression) and rasa (mood). The Sangeet Natak Akademi (1953) recognises eight classical forms; the Ministry of Culture (2000) added Chhau in debate but does not list it. The commonly listed eight: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Kathakali, Sattriya, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam.

• Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu): from Sadir of temple devadasis; Tanjore Quartet (Chinnaiah, Ponniah, Sivanandam, Vadivelu). Alarippu, jatiswaram, varnam, tillana. Revived by E. Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale (Kalakshetra, 1936). Cut off the “devadasi” tag.
  • Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh): Siddhendra Yogi; originally male Brahmin troupes; tarangam (dance on a brass plate).

• Kathak (north India): kathakars (storytellers); Persian influence under the Mughals; gharanas Jaipur, Lucknow, Banaras; tatkar, chakkars; Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi.
  • Odissi (Odisha): temple maharis, Khandagiri-Udayagiri carvings; tribhanga posture; Jayadeva’s Gita Govinda; Kelucharan Mohapatra.

• Kathakali (Kerala): elaborate make-up and costume; stories from the epics; mudras; Vallathol revived it (Kerala Kalamandalam, 1930).
  • Mohiniyattam (Kerala): female solo; lasya style; swaying movements.
  • Sattriya (Assam): Sankardeva (15th century), monasteries (sattras); recognised in 2000.
  • Manipuri: Vaishnava Raslila; soft, lyrical; costume kumil; Ras Leela, Pung cholom.

• Garba, Dandiya (Gujarat); Bhangra, Giddha (Punjab); Lavani, Koli (Maharashtra); Ghoomar, Kalbelia (Rajasthan, Kalbelia in UNESCO ICH list 2010).
  • Bihu (Assam); Chhau (Odisha, Jharkhand, West Bengal; UNESCO 2010); Yakshagana (Karnataka); Theyyam (Kerala); Dollu Kunitha; Karakattam; Garadi; Nati (Himachal).
  • Tribal: Ho, Santhal, Gond, Naga dances.

Sangeet Natak Akademi (1952 inaugurated, 1953 constituted), National School of Drama, Kalakshetra, Kerala Kalamandalam, Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards, Padma awards. UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage: Kutiyattam (2008), Chhau (2010), Kalbelia (2010), Garba of Gujarat (inscribed December 2023).

Historians such as Avanthi Meduri and Janet O’Shea examine how the 20th-century nationalist revival “classicised” Sadir by removing devadasis from the stage and promoting a respectable Brahmanical image. Critics say this erased hereditary women artists. Others credit Rukmini Devi with saving the art.

Dance is soft power: ICCR and Indian missions send troupes abroad. Garba’s UNESCO listing, Yoga Day and Padma awards to folk artists show state support. Livelihood concerns of folk artists and the ban on dancing in public have been debated; Sangeet Natak Akademi offers pensions to senior artists.

  • Prelims tip: Sattriya = Assam, Sankardeva; Kuchipudi = Andhra; Mohiniyattam = Kerala female; Odissi = Odisha, tribhanga; Chhau and Kalbelia = UNESCO lists.
